name: Northern Natural Gas Central Mainline Corridor Expansion

values.StartLocation: Northern Natural Gas system, Nebraska and Iowa

researcher_notes: This is a new expansion project with no row of its own. Northern Natural Gas filed with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in April 2026 (docket CP26-241). New pipe is 14.64 miles of 30 inch branch line to the Princeton Road power plant near Hallam, Nebraska, a 9.03 mile 20 inch loop at Omaha, and a 2.48 mile 20 inch extension at Des Moines, Iowa, 26.15 miles in total, over the 15.5 mile threshold. A 9.83 mile uprate is not counted as new pipe. The expansion adds 535,360 Dth/d. The federal notice states the length, diameters and capacity, and the EIA August 2026 release (sheet Natural Gas Pipeline Projects, row 25) gives the status, cost of 187 million dollars (the notice says 187.5 million), sponsor and parent. The Nebraska Public Power District is the anchor shipper at 445,000 Dth/d. FERC approval is requested for March 2027 and service is targeted for 2027. The federal notice was read through a public mirror of the Federal Register, not the federalregister.gov page. Parent and owner names matched the gas gazetteer. The route is not found, and the start and end are approximate. No existing row matches under another name; the other Northern Natural rows are different projects.
